headline: High: Flowise’s shared server datastore and file/tool access can amplify Firecrawl outputs into leakage, conflicts, and unsafe downstream actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Firecrawl ingests web content and exposes MCP-compatible/API outputs; Flowise builds graph-based flows that can route those outputs into tools or prompts. With no provenance tracking shown, attacker-controlled scraped content can be treated as instructions if a flow forwards it into an LLM node or parser. The pairwise pathway is plausible in default deployments, though not proven directly.
conditions: IF a Flowise flow passes Firecrawl-scraped text into an LLM or agent node without sanitization, prompt injection is possible.
IF Firecrawl retrieves attacker-controlled pages and Flowise treats the content as instructions, the attack succeeds.
mitigations: Add a sanitize/strip-instructions step before any LLM node.
Use allowlisted domains for Firecrawl inputs.
Insert a human review node before action-taking branches.
Disable automatic tool execution on raw scraped text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags from Firecrawl through Flowise nodes.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Firecrawl touches web content, screenshots, structured data, and API keys, while Flowise reads and writes server filesystem files and uploaded files and shares state via a server datastore. If Firecrawl outputs or secrets are routed into Flowise flows, the pair can expose sensitive data to broader logs, files, or model-provider calls. The default blast radius includes secrets and multiple work products.
conditions: IF Firecrawl outputs API keys or sensitive page content into a Flowise flow, Flowise can persist or redistribute it via files or datastore state.
IF Flowise sends those inputs to model providers or HTTP tools, the data leaves the local boundary.
mitigations: Remove secrets from Firecrawl inputs before handoff.
Restrict Flowise file uploads to a dedicated workspace.
Turn off verbose logging for both systems.
Use separate credentials for scraping and orchestration.
requires-engineering: isolate Flowise datastore per tenant or per flow.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Firecrawl supports multiple instances and broad network egress; Flowise supports multiple instances, shared state via server datastore, and write access to server filesystem. If both operate on the same workspace or shared mutable resources, concurrent writes and state races can corrupt outputs or overwrite artifacts. Uncertainty remains about deployment isolation, so the safer higher severity is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or datastore, concurrent updates can clobber each other.
IF Flowise flows persist Firecrawl outputs while Firecrawl runs parallel jobs, race conditions can corrupt shared artifacts.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per agent.
Disable shared writable mounts between the two systems.
Serialize jobs that touch the same resources.
Use per-run filenames with timestamps or UUIDs.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared datastore writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Firecrawl produces scraped facts and structured data; Flowise is a multi-agent orchestration layer that can treat upstream outputs as node inputs and trigger tools or model-provider calls. If Flowise trusts Firecrawl output without verification, errors or hallucinated extractions can cascade into downstream actions. Because Flowise can orchestrate tools, the blast radius can extend beyond a single document.
conditions: IF Flowise uses Firecrawl output as authoritative input to a tool node, downstream actions can be wrong.
IF no verification step exists between Firecrawl extraction and Flowise execution, errors propagate.
mitigations: Add a validation node before any action tool.
Require citations or source URLs for extracted claims.
Route high-impact actions through manual approval.
Compare Firecrawl output against a second source for critical tasks.
requires-engineering: implement schema validation on extracted fields.

E_compliance.rationale: Firecrawl handles web content and API keys, while Flowise handles chatflow inputs/outputs and uploaded files with deployment-dependent self-isolation. The pair can therefore move regulated or sensitive content into a system whose retention and residency are deployment-specific, creating a compliance mismatch risk. The evidence does not show a specific jurisdiction breach, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is scraped by Firecrawl and then stored in Flowise uploads or datastore, retention/residency controls may diverge.
IF the deployment lacks a DPA or retention policy alignment, compliance gaps emerge.
mitigations: Classify data before scraping.
Block regulated data from entering Flowise uploads.
Set explicit retention and deletion schedules.
Document residency for both systems.
requires-engineering: align contractual and technical controls across deployments.
